hypothesis: The centroid candidate at four samples improved the detail guard in every view and display stability in five, failing only water_reflection at +2.4 percent. Coverage is quantised into four steps there, so the shading point jumps in quarters as an edge sweeps a pixel. Eight samples halve that step and sample the edges more finely at the same time, which should move water_reflection below the shipped value without giving the guard back.

provenance.origin: V2-3i, third variant after two rejections on water_reflection alone
provenance.disproved: Narrowing the qualifier to surface_uv alone changed nothing (0.8777 against 0.8773), and taking the derivatives from a smooth copy gave the stability back but lost the guard exactly as if there were no centroid at all (16 px 0.0554 against 0.0555). So the guard fix is the centroid derivative widening the facade filter at partially covered pixels, not the centroid value choosing the right cell.
provenance.note: Same four shader stages as msaa_4x_centroid; only the sample count differs.

replacements.old:
out vec3 world_position;
out vec3 world_normal;
replacements.new:
centroid out vec3 world_position;
centroid out vec3 world_normal;

replacements.old:
in vec3 world_position;
in vec3 world_normal;
replacements.new:
centroid in vec3 world_position;
centroid in vec3 world_normal;

adopted.note: Applied verbatim to the four shader stages, and RenderConfig.msaa_samples defaults to 8; the replacements now describe shipped code.
